key_plays: Q4 12:55: Bryce Underwood threw a 6-yard touchdown pass to Mason Bonner; Jacob Baggett’s kick put Michigan ahead 10-3.
Q4 0:10: Anthony Woods threw a 1-yard touchdown pass to Brayden Loftin, tying the game 10-10 for UCLA.
OT: Mateen Bhaghani made a 38-yard field goal for UCLA; Jacob Baggett answered with a 29-yard field goal for Michigan, making it 13-13.
2OT: Jacob Baggett made a 52-yard field goal, then Mateen Bhaghani’s 38-yarder tied it 16-16.
3OT: Bryce Underwood passed to Jalen Hoffman for the winning two-point conversion, giving Michigan an 18-16 victory.
content.storyline: Michigan upset previously unbeaten No. 4 UCLA in triple overtime, ending the Bruins’ 10-0 start and handing them their first loss. The win made Michigan bowl eligible at 6-5.

recap.paragraph: In Michigan, the Wolverines faced unbeaten No. 4 UCLA with a bowl trip at stake. Bryce Underwood tossed a touchdown to Mason Bonner for a 10-3 lead. UCLA tied it with 10 seconds left. The teams traded kicks through 2 overtimes. Then Underwood found Jalen Hoffman for the winning 2-point conversion! Michigan stunned UCLA 18-16 in a triple-overtime upset. The win made Michigan bowl eligible at 6-5.
